ideas.title: Identity Over Outcome
ideas.body: Lasting change starts with who you decide to become, not the result you're chasing. Every small habit is a vote for a certain kind of person.

ideas.title: The Four Laws
ideas.body: Make cues obvious, cravings attractive, actions easy, and rewards satisfying. Reverse each law to break a habit instead of building one.

ideas.title: 1% Better
ideas.body: Tiny, consistent improvements compound over months into results that feel sudden but were actually earned daily.

ideas.title: Environment Design
ideas.body: Willpower is overrated. Shape your surroundings so the good choice becomes the easy, obvious one.

ideas.title: Never Miss Twice
ideas.body: One slip is an accident. Two in a row is the start of a new habit — get back on track immediately.

ideas.title: Shared Fictions
ideas.body: Humans lead the planet because we believe in things that exist only in imagination — money, nations, laws — and cooperate at scale because of it.

ideas.title: The Cognitive Revolution
ideas.body: A rewiring of the human mind gave us flexible language, letting rumors, myths, and plans spread across entire tribes.

ideas.title: The Agricultural Trap
ideas.body: Farming didn't liberate humanity — it tied people to land and often meant harder lives for the many, surplus for the few.

ideas.title: Money as Trust
ideas.body: Currency is the most universal story ever told — a system of mutual trust that lets total strangers cooperate.

ideas.title: The Unhappiness Question
ideas.body: Progress in power hasn't guaranteed progress in wellbeing. History's biggest gains didn't always make individual lives better.

ideas.title: The Deep Work Hypothesis
ideas.body: The ability to focus without distraction is becoming rare and valuable — those who cultivate it will thrive.

ideas.title: Attention Residue
ideas.body: Switching tasks leaves mental residue that drags down performance on whatever comes next. Batching beats multitasking.

ideas.title: Rituals Over Willpower
ideas.body: Fixed routines around when and where you do deep work remove decision fatigue and make focus automatic.

ideas.title: Embrace Boredom
ideas.body: Constant stimulation trains your brain to crave distraction. Practicing stillness rebuilds your capacity to concentrate.

ideas.title: Judge Your Tools
ideas.body: Evaluate apps and platforms by whether they serve your core goals, not by the fear of missing out.

ideas.title: Two Systems
ideas.body: System 1 is fast, intuitive, emotional. System 2 is slow and deliberate. Most of daily life runs on System 1 — for better and worse.

ideas.title: Anchoring
ideas.body: An early number, even an irrelevant one, quietly shapes every estimate that follows it.

ideas.title: Loss Aversion
ideas.body: Losses hurt roughly twice as much as equivalent gains feel good, which explains why people avoid reasonable risks.

ideas.title: The Availability Heuristic
ideas.body: We judge how common something is by how easily examples come to mind, not by actual frequency.

ideas.title: Planning Fallacy
ideas.body: We reliably underestimate how long tasks will take, even when we know the pattern from experience.

ideas.title: Seek Wealth, Not Money
ideas.body: Wealth is owning assets that earn while you sleep. Money is just a social IOU for time and value.

ideas.title: Specific Knowledge
ideas.body: Skills built through genuine curiosity can't be trained by anyone else — no one can outsource or automate them.

ideas.title: Play Long-Term Games
ideas.body: Compounding, in relationships, knowledge, and money, rewards the people who simply stay in the game longest.

ideas.title: Judgment Over Effort
ideas.body: In an age of leverage, good judgment matters more than hours worked. Think clearly before acting quickly.

ideas.title: Happiness Is a Skill
ideas.body: Peace comes from wanting what you already have — practiced deliberately, like any other skill.
